text:
kai brown: Quick idea drop: what if breadcrumbs include a tiny permalink inspector (hover or keyboard) that shows whether the current URL is canonical or a legacy shortlink, and offers "Copy canonical link" + "Open original". Prototype sketch: https://sketch.redwood/permalink-inspector. Thoughts on UX + routing impact?

jun park: interesting. this would make migrations less mysterious for users. question: do we want to surface "legacy" status to users or hide it and silently canonicalize?

elaine wu: UX: show the inspector only on demand (hover/focus) to avoid UI noise. Label the badge: "Link status: canonical" or "Legacy link (redirected)". For copy button aria-label use "Copy canonical link to clipboard". Keep text brief.

mike cole: infra implications: two approaches: 1) server 301 redirects -> external link clients get canonical; 2) silent client-side rewrite using replaceState. If we surface legacy status, server needs to set an X-Redirect-Source header so client can show inspector state without extra roundtrip. Example: 
```
// server
if (isLegacy(req.path)) {
  res.setHeader('X-Redirect-Source', req.originalUrl)
  res.redirect(301, canonical + req.url.search + req.url.hash)
}
```

samir (sam): accessibility: inspector must be reachable by keyboard (e.g., via breadcrumb focus then press 'i' or via a small button). Announce status changes with aria-live polite, and ensure the Copy button is reachable and announces "Link copied" with role=status. Also consider a tooltip fallback for screen readers.

priya rao: docs + support: exposing "legacy" might confuse external users. We should include a short help doc and release note lines. Also if we add shortlink service, we'll need to document retention policies.

zoe kim: visual: tiny status dot + text works. When legacy, use subtle orange; when canonical, green. Also add an optional "Why was I redirected?" link in the inspector that opens a modal with one-liner. Keep it dismissible and not auto-opening.

kai brown: product question: do we want a shortlink service (eg redwood.app/s/abc) that maps to canonical paths? pros: stable public links, easy for partners. cons: additional infra and abuse surface. open to hear infra view.

mike cole: shortlink service is doable. we'll need a lookup table and TTLs for entries, rate limits, and audit logs. Could use a small redirect microservice. Ticket: PLAT-4333 to explore pros/cons and propose an implementation.

jun park: behavior decision: prefer server-side 301 for external user agents (SEO + link sharing), but client-side replaceState when navigating inside the app to avoid extra navigation flicker and history noise. Inspector UI can read X-Redirect-Source for display.

elaine wu: agree. UX: if inspector shows "Legacy link (redirected)" give an inline "Copy canonical" CTA so power users can grab the stable URL. Keep language non-technical: "This link points to an older path. Open canonical link".

samir (sam): keyboard shortcut suggestion: when breadcrumb focused, offer Ctrl+Shift+C (Windows) / Cmd+Shift+C (Mac) to copy canonical. But double-check conflicts. Also add tests: screen reader sees inspector, copy announces status, focus management when opening modal. I'll add to a11y checklist.

priya rao: I'll draft support copy and a short FAQ entry. Also recommend we instrument telemetry: permalink_inspector_opened, permalink_copied, permalink_shortlink_created. Include origin: docs|ticket|user.

mike cole: noted. PLAT-4333 will include: redirect header X-Original-Path, shortlink prototype plan, telemetry schema, and replaceState behavior. I'll file and link.

zoe kim: tiny microcopy nit: inspector headline = "Link info"; status label = "Canonical" / "Legacy (redirected)"; copy button = "Copy canonical link". Keep sentence case.

kai brown: consensus: 1) experiment with non-intrusive inspector (focus/hover) 2) server 301 for external hits + replaceState on client nav 3) shortlink exploration ticket (PLAT-4333) 4) a11y + telemetry requirements. Anyone object?

jun park: SGTM. can we also add a graceful fallback: if X-Original-Path missing, we treat as canonical to avoid flicker?

mike cole: yes, treat missing header as canonical. we'll make inspector resilient.

samir (sam): I'll provide exact aria-label strings before the PR so we can review with VoiceOver.

elaine wu: I'll prepare the tiny UI frames and wording for the inspector and small modal. Posting later today.

priya rao: I'll prep the support blurb and coordinate with marketing for the release note line: "Improved permalink handling: inspector for migrated links; legacy URLs continue to work."

kai brown: thanks all. i'll drop the prototype link when it's updated and tag folks. :sparkles:
